# System Composer Properties and Styling Implementation Roadmap

- Status: `completed`
- Updated: `2026-07-24T20:40:50Z`

## Objective

Complete configurable asset properties and deliver bounded reusable styling controls across the System Composer inspector and preview.

## Discovery

The System Composer already persists schema-declared instance configuration and renders it in the shared desktop/thin-client preview, but renderer-visible values are incomplete: all 13 frontend-backed conversation definitions have empty strict configuration schemas while their previews contain fixed titles, labels, sample copy, and accessibility text. The inspector has schema-driven controls but no color picker or system-wide reusable style profile. Foundation v2 is an immutable exact-version release, so completing schemas requires a successor release rather than mutating v2.

### Constraints

- Do not mutate the immutable Foundation v2 manifest, definitions, or backing resources in place.
- Do not expose arbitrary CSS, raw stylesheets, unrestricted dimensions, or free-form style values; store bounded semantic choices and generate allowlisted CSS variables/classes.
- Every renderer-visible configurable value must be declared in the exact asset configuration schema and validated before persistence.
- Reusable system styling and per-asset overrides must participate in existing draft, undo, validation, immutable revision save, reload, preview, and build flows.
- Keep the shared System Composer and preview host-neutral so desktop and thin-client behavior remain aligned.
- Preserve all unrelated uncommitted work in the current worktree.
- Use focused tests while implementing a chunk and defer full applicable repository gates until its increment is complete.

## High-level decisions

### Reusable styling ownership for the successor Foundation release

Where should the bounded reusable style profile live while missing renderer properties are completed in an immutable Foundation v3 release?

Foundation v2 cannot be amended without violating the accepted immutable-release architecture, and strict asset schemas reject undeclared configuration. All options therefore publish a v3 successor for completed property schemas and provide an explicit upgrade path for existing v2 systems. The choice determines how global style values are persisted, validated, inherited by previews, and overridden by individual assets. In every option, users edit semantic tokens through color pickers and allowlisted dropdowns; they do not edit arbitrary CSS text.

- Status: `approved`
- Selected option: `root-instance-theme`

| Option | Summary | Recommended | Tradeoffs | Consequences |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Foundation v3 with a root-instance theme profile (root-instance-theme) | Declare the reusable theme profile on the v3 system-root asset configuration, inherit it through the composed preview tree, and declare bounded per-asset override fields only where relevant. | yes | Reuses the existing selected-configuration, validation, undo, revision-save, reload, and build paths.; Keeps one system-scoped style source without introducing another composition node.; Requires a dedicated Styling editor for a structured root configuration field and an explicit v2-to-v3 upgrade action. | Publish Foundation v3 definitions and backing resources with completed renderer property schemas.; Add allowlisted semantic color, typography, spacing, button, form, and surface tokens to the system root.; Map inherited tokens and per-asset overrides to generated CSS custom properties and stable style-role classes in the shared preview. |
| Foundation v3 with a dedicated theme asset (dedicated-theme-asset) | Represent the reusable style profile as a nonvisual Foundation asset that is bound to the system root and consumed by visual descendants. | no | Makes themes independently reusable and conceptually asset-native.; Adds theme discovery, binding, uniqueness, inheritance, upgrade, and placement semantics to an already complex composition graph.; Requires the inspector to coordinate selection of a visual asset with editing a different bound theme asset. | Publish Foundation v3 property schemas plus a new theme asset definition and binding contract.; Add validation that a visual system has exactly one effective theme binding.; Keep per-asset overrides in each visual asset's declared configuration. |
| Foundation v3 plus a revision-level style profile (revision-native-theme) | Add a style-profile field directly to the System Builder revision contract while using v3 only for the completed per-asset property schemas. | no | Separates system-wide presentation from the root asset and makes theme availability unconditional.; Expands contracts, persistence adapters, use cases, IPC/HTTP clients, import/export, and qualification surfaces.; Duplicates configuration validation concepts outside the Asset Kernel and weakens asset portability. | Migrate every revision transport and persistence path for the new profile.; Maintain a second schema and validator for styling outside asset configuration.; Bridge revision-level tokens into the shared asset preview and build output. |

## Increment 1: Property-complete Foundation v3

- Id: `foundation-v3-property-model`
- Status: `completed`
- Dependencies: None

Publish an immutable successor Foundation release whose frontend-backed assets declare every user-owned preview value and whose root asset declares the bounded reusable theme profile approved in Option A.

### Work packages

- **Presentation property audit and catalog** (`presentation-property-audit`): Every frontend-backed asset has an auditable mapping from rendered content and style roles to a declared configurable property or an explicitly fixed structural label.
- **Foundation v3 schemas and backing resources** (`versioned-foundation-contracts`): Completed configuration schemas, defaults, UI hints, semantic theme tokens, per-asset style overrides, and backing resources are published under a new exact Foundation version without changing v1 or v2.
- **Version registration and compatibility** (`version-coexistence`): The new release is discoverable as current while older exact versions remain resolvable and unchanged.

### Deliverables

- Foundation v3 manifest, definitions, backing resources, and exact-version registration
- Completed conversation and remaining frontend-backed asset property schemas
- Bounded root theme and relevant per-asset override schemas
- Automated presentation-property completeness audit
- Contract, manifest, conformance, and immutability regression tests
- Architecture, Asset Kernel, System Builder, and context documentation updates

### Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Qualification | Latest evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `all-preview-properties-declared`: For every frontend-backed Foundation asset, each renderer-visible user-owned value is represented by a typed schema field and bounded UI hint, while fixed structural labels are explicitly classified and tested. | local | passed (test) |
| `bounded-theme-contract`: The v3 system-root schema declares reusable semantic colors, typography sizes, button styles, form styles, and surface/background roles, and relevant visual assets declare only allowlisted override choices without arbitrary CSS fields. | local | passed (test) |
| `immutable-version-coexistence`: Foundation v1 and v2 fixtures remain byte-for-byte behaviorally unchanged while v3 validates, installs, resolves, and generates complete backing resources by exact version. | local | passed (test) |

### Verification

- Run focused asset contract, Foundation manifest, backing-resource, validation, and property-audit tests while implementing each chunk.
- After all increment chunks complete, run the applicable Asset Kernel/Foundation suites, architecture check, docs check, and agent-support check.

### Rollback

Remove the additive v3 registration and files; v1 and v2 remain untouched and continue to resolve by exact version.

### Excluded

- Arbitrary CSS or stylesheet source editing
- The interactive System Composer sidebar and preview rendering, which are delivered in Increment 2
- Automatic in-place mutation of existing v2 systems

## Increment 2: Cohesive properties, Styling tab, and live preview experience

- Id: `cohesive-styling-editor-preview`
- Status: `completed`
- Dependencies: `foundation-v3-property-model`

Deliver the complete shared System Composer experience for editing all declared asset properties, reusable theme roles, and bounded per-asset overrides with immediate accurate Canvas preview feedback.

### Work packages

- **Properties and Styling editors** (`right-sidebar-experience`): The right sidebar provides Properties, Styling, and Layers & Structure tabs; schema-appropriate pickers and dropdowns replace avoidable free-form inputs.
- **Theme inheritance and per-asset overrides** (`theme-inheritance-and-overrides`): Root style roles inherit through the full composition tree while selected assets can choose bounded overrides relevant to their semantic role.
- **Live Canvas, draft, and revision integration** (`preview-and-draft-integration`): Content and style changes update the Canvas immediately and participate in undo, redo, validation, save, reload, and immutable revision history.

### Deliverables

- Shared Styling sidebar tab and responsive collapsed/normal/maximized behavior
- Color-picker and allowlisted typography, spacing, button, form, and surface controls
- Schema-driven missing content/property controls including the conversation-shell title
- Per-asset semantic style override controls in Properties
- Inherited CSS custom-property and stable style-role preview rendering
- Shared UI interaction, accessibility, persistence, and deterministic preview tests
- Shared UI and System Builder documentation updates

### Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Qualification | Latest evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `complete-bounded-editors`: Every declared user-facing asset property is editable with an appropriate bounded control, including conversation-shell content; colors use color pickers and limited choices use selects rather than unrestricted text fields. | local | passed (test) |
| `reusable-styling-and-overrides`: Users can configure reusable button, form, typography, and primary/secondary/tertiary surface roles in Styling and apply relevant bounded overrides from a selected asset's Properties view. | local | passed (test) |
| `accurate-live-preview`: The full hierarchical Canvas preview reflects content, inherited theme roles, and per-asset overrides without duplicating child UI or exposing executable/raw CSS, and representative reference-preview HTML matches reviewed ideal fixtures. | local | passed (test) |
| `draft-history-roundtrip`: Property and styling changes support undo/redo and survive validated revision save and reload with deterministic output in the shared desktop/thin-client UI. | local | passed (test) |

### Verification

- Run focused inspector, structure-editor, preview-renderer, accessibility, and workspace interaction tests for each completed chunk.
- After all increment chunks complete, run the complete shared System Composer/UI suites plus architecture, docs, agent-support, and relevant TypeScript/build checks.

### Rollback

Remove the additive Styling panel, theme projection, and v3-only editor integrations while leaving the versioned v3 contracts available but unused.

### Excluded

- A general-purpose code or CSS editor
- User-defined CSS selectors or arbitrary numeric dimensions
- Host-specific forks of the shared composer

## Increment 3: Reference-system upgrade and production qualification

- Id: `reference-upgrade-production-qualification`
- Status: `completed`
- Dependencies: `cohesive-styling-editor-preview`

Move current reference-system creation to Foundation v3, provide a non-destructive explicit upgrade path for existing v2 systems, and qualify the complete experience across supported hosts and durable boundaries.

### Work packages

- **Property-complete v3 reference systems** (`reference-system-v3`): New reference systems use v3 assets, meaningful initial property values, and reviewed theme profiles that produce useful deterministic previews.
- **Non-destructive v2-to-v3 upgrade** (`explicit-system-upgrade`): Users can explicitly create a new validated v3 revision from an existing v2 system while the original revision and exact-version references remain intact.
- **Cross-host and durable-boundary qualification** (`host-and-boundary-qualification`): Desktop and thin-client hosts, persistence, import/export, build/test output, and reference-preview fixtures agree on the completed property and style semantics.

### Deliverables

- Foundation v3 reference templates and default style profiles
- Explicit upgrade use case, shared UI action, validation, and revision mapping
- Backward-compatibility coverage for existing v1/v2 systems
- Desktop/thin-client, persistence, import/export, and build-output regression coverage
- Reference preview ideal-HTML fixtures and comparison tests
- Final architecture, operations, user, and context documentation

### Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Qualification | Latest evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `new-reference-systems-use-v3`: Every newly created reference system selects Foundation v3, has a valid root theme profile and meaningful configurable content defaults, and renders the reviewed deterministic preview structure. | local | passed (test) |
| `upgrade-is-explicit-and-nondestructive`: Upgrading an existing v2 system is an explicit user action that creates a new validated v3 revision, preserves the prior revision, maps supported configuration and composition data, and reports any unmapped value before save. | local | passed (test) |
| `supported-boundaries-roundtrip`: V3 properties and styling round-trip through supported desktop/thin-client clients, persistence, import/export, and build/test output while v1/v2 systems continue to load by exact version. | local | passed (test) |
| `production-gates-pass`: Applicable repository test, architecture, documentation, agent-support, server-build, thin-client-build, and desktop TypeScript/package qualification gates pass or any environment-only limitation is explicitly reported with focused evidence passing. | local | passed (test) |

### Verification

- Run focused reference-template, upgrade, persistence, import/export, host-contract, and preview-fixture tests while implementing each chunk.
- After all increment chunks complete, run npm test and all applicable repository architecture, documentation, agent-support, server, thin-client, and desktop build/package gates.

### Rollback

Stop advertising v3 as current and remove the additive upgrade action; exact v1/v2 systems remain loadable and their saved revisions are unchanged.

### Excluded

- Automatic migration without user confirmation
- Mutation or deletion of historical system revisions
- Redesign of unrelated Asset Library or System Manage experiences
